lines.text: Tiny sensors in your skin feel the air cool… and quietly let your brain know.
Your brain answers in two soft steps.
First, the little blood vessels near your skin narrow. Warm blood stays deeper inside you.
Then, if you're cold… your muscles begin to tremble. Not on purpose. Tiny, quick tightenings, over and over.
They do just one thing. They make heat. A strong shiver makes several times more than your body makes at rest.
And goosebumps? The same signal reaches the tiny muscle beside each hair… and lifts it upright.
One cool breeze. Skin, nerves, vessels and muscle, all answering together. All… without asking you.
